title: Why Your AI Agent Needs a Wallet: USDC and Nanopayments — Harshal Bhangale, Circle
talk_summary: A Circle engineer pitches giving AI agents USDC wallets so they can autonomously pay for premium APIs via x402/HTTP 402 pay-per-request flows, with wallet-enforced spending guardrails instead of human approval per transaction. The demo contrasts a vanilla Claude Code agent that stalls at paywalled/unsupported actions (email send, phone call) with a wallet-equipped agent that pays providers and completes the task.

takeaways.technique: Pay-per-call capability providers instead of account/API-key setup
takeaways.what_they_do: When an agent hits a capability it lacks (send email, place call, premium data), it pays a third-party provider per request rather than requiring a human to provision an account or key.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent just does not have the ability uh it cannot send out an email natively ... whereas the other agent ... will just be able to use um a provider, pay it, and send an email

takeaways.technique: Spend guardrails enforced at the credential/wallet layer, not per-action approval
takeaways.what_they_do: Caps (max per session, max per day) live in the wallet so the agent can transact autonomously within limits without a human approving each small payment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you sort of build these guardrails into the wallet. And you don't have to as a human approve every single transaction
takeaways.numbers: demo guardrail: max 15 cents per call
